newsitem.title: UK: Phillips to appeal Enron J-Block judgement.
newsitem.headline: Phillips to appeal Enron J-Block judgement.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co will be applying to the UK's House of Lords for leave to appeal a decision in Enron Corp's favour in the Court of Appeal in London, a spokesman for the company told Reuters on Thursday.

The Court of Appeal reversed an earlier ruling made on May 9 which held that Enron could not refuse to agree an early start date for its J-Block contract unless it had operational and technical reasons for doing so.

The Phillips representative pointed out that the Court of Appeal overturned the original May 9 decision by two to one, and said the company is now consulting with its partners in the J-block to decide how to proceed.

Enron has a long-term "take or pay contract" to buy natural gas from the North Sea's J-block, agreed with producers Phillips (36.5 percent, operator), Agip (UK) Ltd (33 percent) and British Gas Exploration and Production Ltd (30.5 percent).

But it told the producers that because of the slump in gas prices on the UK's spot market, it would not take delivery of gas before September 30, 1998. It also refused to agree a Commissioning Date, so seeking to defer the start of its take or pay obligations.

Phillips won a victory in the High Court in May when the court ruled that Enron could not refuse to agree a Commissioning Date. This is the ruling that has now been overturned and which Phillips says it will be appealing.
